fields.description:
Found while verifying d724 AC10 against Windows sweep 35551741150.

tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_signing_key_keeps_restrictive_mode asserts the signing key is mode 0o600. Windows reports 0o666 because it does not implement POSIX permission bits, so the assertion can never hold there.

Needs a decision rather than a mechanical fix: either the test asserts POSIX-only and is skipped on Windows, or rebar owes a real Windows ACL equivalent for signing-key confidentiality. The second reading is a genuine security question, not a test-portability one, and should be settled before the test is silenced.

Not the d724 defect class.

## Verification (2026-10-24, current main)
The test named above, `test_signing_key_keeps_restrictive_mode`, no longer exists: commit 3beb7e4ad23 (Retire the legacy HMAC-SHA256 signing scheme) deleted it. The same POSIX-only assertion survives at `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py:212`, inside `test_opcert_signing_key_is_isolated_per_store`: `assert all((key.stat().st_mode & 0o777) == 0o600 for key in copy_keys)`. The Windows value (0o666) is as reported in the ticket's sweep run; it has not been re-measured here.

## Decision (operator, 2026-10-24)
Skip the permission-bit assertion where the platform does not implement POSIX permission bits, and track the confidentiality question separately. The operator chose this over implementing Windows ACL restriction first.

## Approach
1. Move the mode assertion out of `test_opcert_signing_key_is_isolated_per_store` into its own test, so the isolation assertions (distinct private and public keys per copy) keep running on every platform.
2. Guard the new test on the capability it needs, not on `os.name`: a helper writes a scratch file, chmods it 0o600, and reads the mode back; the test skips when the read-back is not 0o600. The skip reason names the missing capability and the follow-up task that owns the Windows confidentiality question.
3. Create that follow-up task (linked `discovered_from`).

## Scope
In scope: `tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py`. Out of scope: any change to how the signing key is written, and Windows ACL handling.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q
make verify
```
On this host the new test must run and pass. The skip path is exercised in a scratch copy of the module whose probe is forced to report no POSIX bits, expecting 1 skipped with the reason. Failure case: with the probe forced false the assertion must not run, and with it true a 0o666 key must still fail the test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The mode assertion no longer sits in `test_opcert_signing_key_is_isolated_per_store`, and that test still asserts key isolation (checked: diff and `pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -q`).
- [x] A separate test asserts mode 0o600 and skips with a reason naming the missing capability when the platform does not honour POSIX permission bits (checked: scratch copy with the probe forced false reports 1 skipped; on this host it passes).
- [x] The guard keys on observed chmod behaviour, not `os.name` or `sys.platform` (checked: review of the diff).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).

## Follow-up
Whether rebar owes a Windows ACL equivalent for signing-key confidentiality is a separate security decision, tracked in its own task so this bug closes on the test portability it actually fixes.
